title: Freezer signer composition is mandated as a fixed inter-organizational split that the parties may rotate themselves
content:
Each freezer multisig has a Modification clause with the same construction. For Ethereum (A.4.2.2.1.5), the Core Facilitator and Core GovOps "can change the signers ... so long as" there are five signers, two are required to execute, two are controlled by the Core Facilitator, and three by Core GovOps. Solana (A.4.2.2.2.3.1.1.5) requires four signers with "an equal number ... controlled by" Soter Labs and Endgame Edge; Avalanche (A.4.2.2.3.3.1.1.5) fixes 2 Soter / 2 Endgame Edge / 1 Grove; Plasma (A.4.2.2.4.3.1.1.5) fixes 3 Soter / 1 Redline / 1 Osero.

The pattern is a delegation bounded by an invariant. Key rotation is operationally routine — staff change, devices are lost, keys are compromised — and routing every rotation through an Executive Vote would either slow security hygiene to a crawl or produce stale signer sets that nobody wants to admit to. So the Atlas delegates the *action* while constitutionalizing the *shape*: who holds how many seats is governance's decision, which specific addresses hold them is operations'.

What the invariant protects is the multi-organizational character of the set. No party can quietly grow its share, and no party can shrink another's, because the allocation is written into the ruleset rather than into the multisig's own configuration.

Notably, the entities empowered to change the signers are exactly the entities that hold the seats. The set is self-administering within its constraints, with the Atlas text — not a supervising body — doing the constraining.
description: Modification clauses let the controlling entities swap keys without a vote, provided the seat count, threshold and per-organization allocation are preserved — an invariant replaces an approval step.
